population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling: ever 35.5% − current 24.9% = 10.6% used-and-off-now; ≈11.0 pts of current users are on a second or later course and ≈3.6 pts of the off-now group restarted at least once before stopping again, so (11.0+3.6)/35.5 ≈ 41%, consistent with ~35–40% one-year persistence (public gated plans ~45%) and ~40% restart within a year. Of ≈274M adults: ≈68.3M current, ≈29.0M used-and-off, ≈177M never used. Age check: 18–29 13% × 52M = 6.8M; 30–49 27% × 90M = 24.3M; 50–64 37% × 62M = 22.9M; 65+ 20.5% × 70M = 14.35M; total ≈ 68.35M ≈ 24.9%. Growth of ≈28.9M users by payer: Medicare +9.4M (6.3→15.7M), Medicaid +7.1M (3.5→10.6M), commercial +4.7M (18.5→23.2M), cash/direct +3.1M (7.9→11.0M), imported/counterfeit/research-peptide +4.7M (3.1→7.8M). The 65+ band more than doubled (8.5%→20.5%) because the Jan 2032 Bridge agreement widened eligibility to label criteria; it would be higher but DEXA waits and the counselling-visit requirement delay starts by 2–4 months. The bottom third (10.3%→22.2%) rose most, through Medicaid in ~30 states and through gray product, which is undercounted. The ~177M never-users are disproportionately under 30, uninsured in non-covering states (Texas, Florida, Georgia adults), or refusers by conviction, now an organised minority. Off-now people (29M) include ~6M who lost gated coverage, ~3M on DEXA-advised or medical pauses, and ~2M who quit citing 'the grey'. Pediatric: 1.3% of ≈73M under-18s ≈ 950k: ≈790k adolescents 12–17 and ≈160k children 6–11 since the June 2031 Wegovy approval, ~60% via Medicaid/CHIP, where EPSDT obliges coverage even in states that exclude adult weight-loss drugs. Roughly a third of US children now live with at least one parent currently on an incretin.

access.public_coverage: Medicare is now the single largest public purchaser. The 2032–34 Bridge successor agreement (signed Nov 2031) sets $179/month for semaglutide and tirzepatide (orals $149–179), keeps the $50 beneficiary copay and the counselling visit, and widens eligibility from BMI-plus-comorbidity to label criteria (BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with one weight-related condition). Medicare users ≈15.7M (23.0% of fills): ≈7.1M via Part D diabetes and ≈8.6M via the Bridge for obesity. Bridge 2032: 8.6M × $179 × 12 ≈ $18.5B gross; beneficiary copays 8.6M × $50 × 12 ≈ $5.2B; net federal ≈ $13.3B. Medicaid ≈10.6M adults (15.5% of fills) in ~30 covering states at the $179 rate: 10.6M × $179 × 12 ≈ $22.8B gross federal+state before supplemental rebates; plus ≈0.57M children under EPSDT: 0.57M × $179 × 12 ≈ $1.2B. Public share of fills 38.5% versus commercial 34.0%. Retatrutide, amycretin, MariTide and Kinetra are not on the Bridge rate; Part D plans cover them only by exception.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide and first tirzepatide-copy brands at $4–25/month. China: generic semaglutide and tirzepatide, and Chinese API for retatrutide and cagrilintide sold as 'research peptides'. Canada: generic semaglutide CAD 45–70. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey, Egypt and Gulf states have generics. EU semaglutide exclusivity ends 2031–32 in most member states; first EU generics launched in late 2032. US: patent settlements with ANDA filers plus six months' pediatric exclusivity from the under-12 approval set the earliest US semaglutide generic entry at 2033.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline continues. Federal direct portal (launched as TrumpRx): injectable semaglutide $179, tirzepatide $179–249, retatrutide $349, oral starting doses $149, higher oral doses $179. Kinetra (tirzepatide + bimagrumab) list is $1,799, with $449 direct. Wegovy list is still $1,349, and almost nobody pays it. Payer mix of ≈68.3M users: commercial 34.0% (23.2M), Medicare 23.0% (15.7M), Medicaid 15.5% (10.6M), cash/direct 16.1% (11.0M, including ≈2.5M 'calm'/'craving' subscribers), imported/counterfeit/research-peptide 11.4% (7.8M) = 100%. The gray 7.8M splits into ≈3.9M mail-order Indian/Chinese generic, ≈2.6M 'research' retatrutide, cagrilintide and 'muscle-sparing stack' vials via offshore-hosted telehealth peptide clinics with US-licensed prescribers, and ≈1.3M counterfeit branded pens via social sellers and med-spas. About 72% of covering employers gate. Two of the big three PBMs added a 90-day 'medical pause' code in 2031 so DEXA-advised pauses no longer forfeit coverage; the third has not, and Medicaid waivers have no such code.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic, incl. 7.2 mg; Wegovy now labelled 6+)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
Unimolecular GLP-1/amylin agonist, weekly injectable (amycretin, approved Nov 2031)
GLP-1 agonist/GIPR antagonist antibody-peptide conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide, approved Jul 2031)
GIP/GLP-1 agonist + activin type II receptor antibody combination (Kinetra: weekly tirzepatide pen plus monthly subcutaneous bimagrumab, approved Mar 2032)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics; labelled 6+ for pediatric use)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (semaglutide, Jun 2031; liraglutide, Oct 2031)
obesity with preservation of lean mass in adults (Kinetra label claim on body composition, not on fractures or falls)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: low-dose 'calm' and 'craving' subscriptions (now sold as 'dose-flex' with built-in holidays after the anhedonia label)
smoking and vaping cessation (new semaglutide trial ongoing; no resubmission)
longevity and 'metabolic health' regimens; Kinetra off-label in normal-weight older adults for 'muscle insurance'
pediatric use under 6 under specialist care, rare
gray 'retatrutide microdosing' for focus among under-30s
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Approvals this window: MariTide (filed Apr 2030, approved Jul 2031, monthly; slow uptake, nausea-limited); amycretin (DEXA data delivered, approved Nov 2031); semaglutide 6–11 (Jun 2031) and liraglutide 6–11 (Oct 2031), with postmarketing bone-accrual and growth-velocity requirements because adolescent bone-accrual results (interim 2-year readout, 2031) were underpowered and inconclusive. Kinetra: the bimagrumab + tirzepatide phase 3 that began in 2029 read out in late 2030, Lilly filed the BLA in Feb 2031, and FDA approved it in Mar 2032 (13 months after filing). Trial: ~22% weight loss with lean mass ~10–12% of loss versus ~35% on tirzepatide alone. No fracture, fall or function endpoint; the label says so. Survodutide resubmission accepted, decision 2033. Oral amycretin and semaglutide-bimagrumab combinations are in phase 3 and not on the US market. Incretin market ≈$131B in 2032: US volume up ~70% on 2030, US net price down a further ~10%, ex-US and EU revenue eroding as generics arrive.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the commonest effect and leading voluntary stop reason. MariTide's monthly dosing front-loads nausea. Worse with unsupervised research-vial escalation.
Elevated with rapid loss; more absolute cases as 65+ uptake doubled.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low; research-vial and counterfeit cases confound reporting.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; MDL litigation ongoing, first bellwether trial set for 2033.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Unchanged on legacy molecules: lean loss ~30–40% of weight lost in untrained users over 50. Kinetra cuts this to ~10–12% in trials, but ~85% of 65+ users are on Bridge-rate semaglutide or tirzepatide, which Kinetra does not replace for them. The marketing line that skinny-frail is 'solved' fits commercial and cash users far better than Medicare ones.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 2028 class label retained; 2029 joint guidance retained; Kinetra label carries a body-composition claim but no function, fall or fracture claim. FDA warning letter (Jul 2032) to a telehealth brand advertising gray 'Kinetra-style stacks'.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: With ≈5M 65+ users on >2 years by 2032, ~0.6%/yr baseline hip-fracture rate × 0.35 excess ≈ 10,500 excess hip fractures a year against ~300,000 total, roughly double 2030's figure from volume alone. The cycling signal in postmenopausal women 50–64 is replicated. Bimagrumab's bone effect is neutral to slightly positive in trial DEXA, unproven for fracture. Medicare DEXA claims up a further ~55%; median regional waits 6–14 weeks.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelling and 2029 joint guidance retained; FDA still requires bone endpoints in new filings (applied to amycretin and Kinetra). DOJ civil matter against Novo from the 2029 HELP referral unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention; no class determination.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association; the anhedonia label explicitly distinguishes reward blunting from suicidality.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', 'the grey', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Oct 2031 class labelling, from pooled trial SHAPS/PHQ items plus the retatrutide postmarketing study, gives dose-tiered estimates of clinically meaningful anhedonia: retatrutide 12 mg 9% vs 4% comparator; tirzepatide 15 mg 5% vs 3%; semaglutide 2.4–7.2 mg 4% vs 3%; low oral doses not distinguishable from comparator. Applied to the 2032 dose mix, the drug-attributable excess is ≈1.5 pts of users, ≈1M Americans. Usually reverses within 4–8 weeks of dose reduction. Pediatric data absent.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Adverse Reactions section for all incretins; Warnings and Precautions for retatrutide with recommendation to assess pleasure/mood at dose escalation. FTC cites the label in 2032 letters to 'calm' brands. No REMS.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Substantial regain within a year. ≈29M adults are off now; involuntary stops from gating and Medicaid waiver misses, DEXA pauses, and grey-driven quits are the main categories.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly. Indiana waiver case still pending in the Seventh Circuit.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D, calcium and protein signals persist, now also flagged in pediatric growth monitoring.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance (2029) retained; AAP 2031 guidance adds growth-velocity and dietary review for under-12s; no FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~7 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of follow-up for the earliest users. Cycling worse for bone in three cohorts. Adolescent bone-accrual interim (2031) inconclusive; under-12 approval made on weight and metabolic endpoints.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements extended to under-12s (growth velocity, bone accrual, pubertal timing, neurodevelopment).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Resurgent. Poison-centre incretin exposure calls up ~60% on 2030. New pattern: 'research use only' retatrutide and cagrilintide vials, often mislabelled in concentration, prescribed by telehealth peptide clinics. A Mar 2032 cluster of endotoxin-contaminated research retatrutide caused ≈90 hospitalisations for sepsis or abscess in Ohio, Michigan and Indiana, with 2 deaths.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CDC HAN advisory (Mar 2032); FDA import alerts and warning letters at the prior pace; state medical boards discipline a handful of prescribers. No new law, no prosecutions of individuals.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent; transient; more reports from research-vial users who over-escalate.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated in 65+ users >2 years; confounding not yet separated. Kinetra has no fall data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening in Bridge counselling template retained.

safety_ledger.effect: Bimagrumab-related effects (muscle spasm, diarrhoea, acne, transient lipase rise)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New. Muscle spasms in ~20–30% of Kinetra users early in therapy, mostly mild; acne ~10%. Long-term effects of activin-receptor blockade on reproductive hormones and other tissues are unknown beyond trial duration.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; postmarketing long-term safety study required; contraindicated in pregnancy.

safety_ledger.effect: Pediatric growth, puberty and emotional development under 12
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New. ≈160k children 6–11 exposed; no signal reported yet and no systematic anhedonia measurement in children.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements; AAP guidance on growth monitoring.

food_and_beverage.state: With a quarter of adults on drug, US salty-snack volume falls ~4–5% a year in 2031–32, confectionery ~3%, and full-sugar soda ~4%. Packaged-food majors sell or spin off two snack brands and keep consolidating SKUs. The under-12 approval makes children's snack marketing fraught: several brands pull kids' TV and app ads in households flagged as 'family on GLP-1' by retail-media data. Protein, fibre and 'bone-forward' lines keep growing, and heritage 'full portion' brands hold a loyal backlash niche.

alcohol.state: US spirits volume declines for a fifth straight year. Beer is soft among 50–64s. The anhedonia label lets brands pitch 'one good drink' as pleasure retained, and low-ABV aperitifs grow. Tobacco and vape volumes keep falling faster than the pre-incretin trend.

restaurants.state: Traffic flat, spend per cover down. With 65+ uptake doubled, early-bird and buffet formats around The Villages, Florida and Sun City, Arizona close units fastest. Half-portion and 'on/off/holiday' menus are standard. Soul-food 'no-gram' rooms in Atlanta, Memphis and Houston keep thriving with backlash and dose-holiday diners.

apparel.state: Size churn remains the business model; senior and adaptive lines resize as Medicare users lose weight. Plus-size specialists hold on body-sovereignty branding. Children's apparel sees early size-mix shifts in Medicaid-heavy regions.

fitness.state: Still growing on Medicare Advantage strength benefits and DEXA-coaching chains, but split: Kinetra marketing ('the muscle comes in the box') coincides with cancellations of prescribed-lifting packages among commercial users in Scottsdale and Plano. Senior strength classes are oversubscribed.

insurance.state: Employer coverage 66%, with ~72% gated. Pharmacy trend ~+5%. Two PBMs added 90-day medical-pause codes. Kinetra sits behind prior authorisation requiring age ≥50 plus low lean mass on DEXA, which pushes DEXA demand higher. Medicare Advantage plans compete on GLP-1 'concierge' wraparounds. Bone and fall costs are standard lines in GLP-1 actuarial models.

pharma.state: Lilly dominates on tirzepatide, retatrutide, Foundayo and now Kinetra. Novo leans on Medicare semaglutide volume, the pediatric label and EU generic defence; its DOJ matter is open. Amgen's MariTide has slow uptake. US volume is up sharply while US net price falls, and the 2033 semaglutide cliff is priced into valuations. DEXA makers, bone-agent generics and pen-authentication firms keep growing.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: With a quarter of adults on drug and Medicare paying, being on it no longer signals class. How you are on it does. Broad shoulders on a thin frame read as Kinetra or lifting: commercial, cash, cared for. Thin arms and a stoop read as long Bridge-rate use. 'Off' has four readings: DEXA pause, coverage lost, conviction, or 'got the grey'.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The level gradient compressed sharply (top 27.5%, bottom 22.2%) as Medicaid and Medicare widened. The quality gradient widened: the top third gets Kinetra, DEXA and coaching, the bottom third gets Bridge-rate or Medicaid semaglutide with long scan waits, and 2.6M people, skewed young and uninsured, inject research vials from Shenzhen labs.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are smaller and protein-first. Dose-holiday Sundays are common, so the weekly family dinner is again the big meal for people who skip their Friday shot. Church potlucks in the Tulsa–Dallas corridor advertise themselves as 'holiday tables'.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list on/off/holiday and sometimes dose. 'Unmedicated' remains a filter in backlash circles. 'Do you get the grey?' is a standard third-date question.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is medicalised, publicly financed, and contested. The under-12 approval gave the backlash its most potent cause. Black women's wellness collectives in Atlanta oppose Medicaid pediatric outreach in DeKalb County schools as body policing of Black children. A Southern Baptist Convention resolution (Jun 2032) calls children's appetite 'a gift not a diagnosis'. Supplement influencers sell 'kids' metabolic gummies'. The coalition still disagrees on whether adult public coverage is good.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. The Oct 2031 class label gives dose-tiered estimates (retatrutide 12 mg 9% vs 4%; tirzepatide 15 mg 5% vs 3%; semaglutide 4% vs 3%; low oral doses indistinguishable). Applied to the 2032 dose mix, that is ≈1M Americans with drug-attributable clinically meaningful anhedonia, plus far more with subthreshold complaints. Surveys by two health systems find ~30% of users report at least one deliberate dose holiday in the past six months. The ≈2.5M 'calm' subscribers are counted inside the 11.0M cash/direct users. Children are not measured.
interior_life.framing: A side effect everyone knows by name. 'The grey' is on the label in clinical language and in common speech. 'Calm' brands rebranded to 'dose-flex' with scheduled holidays. Clinicians titrate to 'lowest dose that holds weight and keeps pleasure'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Dose holidays collide with gating: proportion-of-days-covered rules count a skipped week, so workers time holidays around the 80% threshold, and HR benefit FAQs explain how. Sales, hospitality and creative workers drop doses before peak periods. Tech lifestyle accounts still reimburse dose-flex subscriptions. Some fleets bar holidays for drivers whose sleep-apnea compliance depends on weight.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Written unmedicated' or 'written on holiday' credits are common in Nashville songwriting and stand-up. A streaming drama about a family split over a nine-year-old's prescription is the year's argument starter. Intense-stimulus leisure (hot sauce, loud venues, adventure travel) keeps growing among users.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists use the label's language; 'holiday weekends' are standard advice. Couples counsellors report dose mismatch as a common presenting complaint. Backlash pastors cite the label in marriage sermons.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The 2032 campaign treats incretins as a pocketbook issue (the $179 deal, the 2033 generic date, importation) and a safety issue (research-vial deaths). Both tickets promised to keep the Bridge; neither proposed legal importation. The backlash coalition drew candidate visits in Georgia and Oklahoma over pediatric use. 'Calm voter' turnout claims remain unpublished and unproven.

state.regulatory_posture: No new state action: Congress passed no importation, compounding or gating law; enforcement stayed at the 2030 pace of import alerts, warning letters and parcel seizures, with no prosecutions of individuals. FDA did routine work through ordinary channels: approvals (MariTide, amycretin, Kinetra, pediatric 6–11) and the anhedonia class labelling.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. Public expansion came through contract and ordinary state plan amendments, not statute: the Nov 2031 CMS–manufacturer Bridge successor ($179, label-criteria eligibility, $50 copay, counselling visit) and ~14 additional state Medicaid programs adopting adult coverage at the $179 rate, bringing the total to ~30. Pediatric coverage follows automatically under EPSDT.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged public conditioning: Indiana and Arkansas waivers (≥80% PDC, quarterly verified weigh-ins, two misses = 12 months off). Private gating at ~72% of covering employers. Pharmacy weigh-in kiosks now also log Bridge counselling-visit attendance. No new government monitoring.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still makes tirzepatide a de facto job requirement for some drivers. Army accession policy unchanged and contested. Some fleets add DEXA for drivers over 55.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Chinese API for research-grade retatrutide and cagrilintide is the new congressional talking point. India–US trade talks still treat mail-order pharma as a bargaining chip. EU generic entry widens the price gap visible to Americans. Section 232 tariffs and domestic-capacity credits remain.

events.event: FDA approves Wegovy for children aged 6–11 with obesity, citing weight and metabolic outcomes and requiring postmarketing studies of growth, puberty and bone accrual; the approval earns Novo six months of pediatric exclusivity, and Medicaid programs must cover it under EPSDT; liraglutide follows in October

FDA adds anhedonia and emotional blunting to labelling for all incretin drugs, with dose-tiered estimates of 9% versus 4% on top-dose retatrutide and a warning to assess pleasure at escalation; 'calm' brands rewrite their copy and clinics publish dose-holiday schedules

CMS and Lilly and Novo sign the 2032–34 Medicare Bridge agreement at $179 a month, widening eligibility to label criteria with the $50 copay and counselling visit unchanged; portal injectable prices fall to $179, and about 14 more states add adult Medicaid coverage at the same rate

FDA approves Lilly's Kinetra, a tirzepatide pen co-packaged with monthly bimagrumab, 13 months after its February 2031 filing; it cuts lean-mass loss to about a tenth of weight lost in trials but carries no fracture or fall claim, and launches at $1,799 list, $449 direct, outside the Medicare Bridge rate

CDC health alert after endotoxin-contaminated 'research use only' retatrutide vials, prescribed through offshore-hosted telehealth peptide clinics, are tied to about 90 hospitalisations and two deaths in Ohio, Michigan and Indiana; poison-centre incretin calls are up roughly 60% on 2030

The Southern Baptist Convention passes a resolution calling children's appetite 'a gift, not a diagnosis' days after Atlanta wellness collectives picket a DeKalb County school-based Medicaid enrolment fair offering pediatric GLP-1 referrals

open_tensions: Medicare and Medicaid now finance the largest share of use, but only at the $179 rate for legacy molecules. The muscle-preserving combination sold as solving skinny-frail is a commercial and cash product, so the population most exposed to fractures and falls is the least likely to get it, while DEXA waits grow.

Gray use regrew to ~7.8M, now including next-generation research vials, with fatal contamination clusters. The 2033 US semaglutide generic date and EU generic prices loom, and Congress has neither sealed the mail nor legalised importation.

Anhedonia is labelled and dose holidays are mainstream practice, yet employer gating and the Indiana/Arkansas waivers count skipped doses against proportion-of-days-covered. Children 6–11 are now prescribed a drug whose label warns about pleasure, with no pediatric measurement of it.

The backlash coalition found its strongest cause in pediatric use. Its most effective targets are public programs that disproportionately serve poor and Black families, which pits its body-sovereignty wing against advocates of equal access and leaves the incoming administration's Bridge renewal politically unpredictable.
still_true: No generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is marketed in the US; settlements and pediatric exclusivity put the earliest entry in 2033.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx).

The Indiana and Arkansas Medicaid 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins, with two misses ending coverage for 12 months; the disability-rights litigation is unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed in January 2026 has not returned to Wegovy, Zepbound or Saxenda labels.
Medicare beneficiaries still pay a $50 monthly copay under the Bridge successor and must attend the counselling visit, which includes fall-risk screening.

prose.headline: One in Four, Medicare Pays, and the Label Finally Admits the Grey: America's Appetite Goes Public
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2032 a quarter of American adults are on an incretin drug, and for the first time the largest single source of payment is the government. The change was administrative, not legislative. In November 2031 CMS and the two manufacturers renewed the Medicare Bridge at $179 a month, dropped the old requirement for a second diagnosis, and kept the fifty-dollar copay and the counselling visit. About fourteen more states copied the rate into their Medicaid programs. Medicare now pays for nearly sixteen million users and Medicaid for more than ten million. The share of Americans over sixty-five on the drug has more than doubled. Congress passed nothing, and nobody had to.

The price fell as everyone expected and stopped where everyone expected. Weekly semaglutide and tirzepatide sell for $179 on the federal portal, and the starter pills are still $149. The patents are almost spent. Settlements with generic makers, plus six months of pediatric exclusivity, mean the first American generic semaglutide arrives in 2033. Europe already has its generics, and Americans can read the European prices.

The pediatric exclusivity came with a pediatric approval. Since June 2031 Wegovy has been licensed for children from age six. About a hundred and sixty thousand children under twelve now take it, most through Medicaid, which must cover it for children under the federal rules for child health screening and treatment even in states that refuse it to adults. The adolescent bone studies were too small to settle anything. The FDA approved the under-twelve use on weight and blood-sugar results and asked for growth and puberty data later.

In October 2031 the drugs' quieting effect went on the label. After two years in which wellness brands sold it as calm, the FDA put numbers on it: about nine in a hundred top-dose retatrutide users lose a meaningful amount of pleasure, against four on comparator, with smaller excesses on the older drugs. Across today's mix of doses that is roughly a million people. The effect usually fades when the dose comes down, so people bring it down. Dose holidays are now ordinary practice. Clinics print schedules for them, and HR pages explain how to take one without falling below the eighty-percent adherence line that most employer plans and two state Medicaid programs still enforce. 'The grey' is a phrase grandparents use.

In March Lilly's Kinetra reached pharmacies: tirzepatide paired with a monthly antibody that keeps muscle. In trials, muscle made up about a tenth of the weight lost instead of a third, and the advertising says frailty is solved. The label claims nothing about fractures or falls. Kinetra costs $449 direct and is not on the Medicare rate. The people breaking hips, perhaps ten thousand extra a year now, mostly cannot get it. They wait two or three months for a bone scan.

The cheaper legal market did not shrink the illegal one. Nearly eight million people use product no American regulator has checked. That includes generic pens from India, counterfeit Ozempic, and now 'research use only' retatrutide vials prescribed by telehealth clinics hosted offshore. In March a contaminated batch put ninety people in hospital across Ohio, Michigan and Indiana, and two of them died. Enforcement stayed where it was: import alerts, warning letters, seized parcels.

The backlash found its cause in children. Atlanta's body-sovereignty collectives picketed a school enrolment fair in DeKalb County. The Southern Baptists resolved that a child's appetite is a gift. Both presidential campaigns promised to protect the Bridge. Snack volumes are falling about five percent a year, buffets near The Villages are closing, and Sunday dinners have grown again because Sunday is when people skip the shot.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Lorraine Pruitt, sixty-seven, retired cafeteria manager, Tulsa, wakes at six and does not take her Thursday shot. She marks HOLIDAY on the paper calendar her pharmacist gave her, the one with eighty percent printed across the bottom in red.

At ten she calls about the bone scan again. Week nine. The woman says maybe the eighteenth.

At noon she drives her granddaughter Kaylee, nine, to the pediatric endocrinologist. SoonerCare covers it. The doctor measures Kaylee against the wall, writes a number, and asks whether Kaylee still laughs at things. Kaylee laughs at the question. The doctor writes that down too.

In the parking lot Kaylee asks if her shot is the same as Grandma's. Lorraine says it's the same family.

At three her neighbour Darnell comes over with a cooler bag. Inside are glass vials marked RESEARCH USE ONLY with a QR code. He pays sixty-five dollars a month through an app and asks if she can read the concentration because his glasses are in the truck. She can't, quite. She tells him about Ohio. He says his clinic is a different clinic.

The Bridge counsellor calls at four for the quarterly visit and asks about falls. One, in March, on the porch step. The counsellor mentions Kinetra and says it isn't on her plan.

At six it's Wednesday-night supper at First Baptist, a holiday table. Pastor Glenn blesses the food and says appetite is a gift. Lorraine has a second piece of peach cobbler and it tastes, she thinks, the way cobbler used to taste.

Friday she'll take the shot.

least_plausible_claims.quote: for the first time the largest single source of payment is the government
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the world's own payer mix has commercial at 34.0% (23.2M) and Medicare at 23.0% (15.7M).
